label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
@Kavya, I saw your post yesterday. With people tagging me, I want to own what I got wrong and clear up a few facts. I won’t name either engineer. They did not ask to be part of a public discussion.

We were both in Foundry91 cohort 4, with demo day in March 2026. You’re building SitterNest; I’m building DabbaDost. But you’re also a friend who sat with me till 1am in the Koramangala office, fixing our Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. I haven’t forgotten that, or the help you’ve given me.

First, my mistake: I knew where both engineers worked from day one. I should have called you before making the offers, not after the second offer was accepted. That’s on me. A WhatsApp message after the decision was made was not the conversation I should have had with you.

I also need to put the hiring facts on record, because the version being repeated isn’t what happened.

We posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September. It was open to anyone. One engineer applied on 19 September. The other came through his referral two weeks later. Nobody from our side DMed either of them to recruit them.

Both offers were 22% above their current CTC, not 40%. Both joined on 3 November. We also have an ESOP pool. It’s small, but it’s real and has been on paper since January. The claim that we promised ESOPs we don’t have is not correct.

None of this cancels out the call I should have made. I can stand by how the applications came in and still accept that I handled the conversation with you badly. I’m sorry for that.

There are 11 startups in our batch, hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. This will come up again. I’d suggest one simple cohort rule: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer. Not a request for permission, or a veto over someone’s career. Just a heads-up so a friend doesn’t hear about it after the fact.

I don’t want this to become a fight, or for anyone to pile on either of us. I respect you, Kavya, and I want to have the conversation I should have had earlier.

Coffee or a call is open this week, whenever you’re okay with it.
